title: Cartierness of a fixed Weil divisor is tested on strict local rings
statement:
Let $Y$ be a Noetherian normal scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]: it has a finite affine cover by Noetherian rings, and each local ring is a domain integrally closed in its fraction field. A Weil divisor is a finite sum $E=\sum_j m_j[Z_j]$, where $m_j\in\mathbf Z$ and the $Z_j$ are distinct integral closed subschemes of codimension one. At the generic point of $Z_j$ its coefficient is measured by the normalized discrete valuation of the corresponding one-dimensional normal local ring. A Cartier divisor is a family of local nonzero rational functions whose ratios on overlaps are regular units; it is effective if its equations belong to the local rings. For a geometric point $\bar y$ put $R=\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}$, the strict henselization of $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. Then $R$ is a Noetherian normal local domain. The pullback $E_R$ has coefficient $m_j$ at each height-one prime over the germ of $Z_j$ containing $y$, and coefficient zero elsewhere; this defines the usual pullback of Weil divisors under strict localization. The analogous rule defines pullback to etale neighborhoods, and is compatible with further strict localization.

Fix an integer $a>0$. The Weil divisor $aE$ is Cartier if and only if for every geometric point $\bar y$ there exists $c_{\bar y}\in\operatorname{Frac}(R)^\times$ with $\operatorname{div}_R(c_{\bar y})=aE_R$. Here $\operatorname{div}_R(c)$ is the sum of its normalized height-one valuations. If $E$ is effective, the generators can be taken in $R\setminus\{0\}$; the resulting global Cartier divisor is effective and has support $\bigcup_{m_j\ne0}|Z_j|$. In that case, near every geometric point there is a pointed etale neighborhood on which this effective Cartier divisor has a single non-zero-divisor equation.

source.place: Agent-formulated strict-local consequence of Tags 0EBM (lemma-normal-class-group, rank-one reflexive modules and Weil classes), 0AY6 (lemma-reflexive-over-normal), and 0BE8 (lemma-normal-c1-injective, proof identifying zero valuations with units); faithful-flat local freeness descent: algebra.tex Tag 00O1 (lemma-finite-projective-descends); normality under etale maps: etale.tex Tag 025P (proposition-etale-normal). This is the precise local test used in ILO VIII 5.3.8, p.125, not a verbatim Stacks lemma.

proof.text: Put $D=aE$. Apply the clopen-component result with the identity etale map of $Y$. Normality means all local rings are reduced domains, so each open irreducible component is integral. Thus we may cover $Y$ by integral affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A$ Noetherian normal. On each $U$ form the concrete module $I_A(D|_U)$ of the divisorial-lattice lemma. Its localization rule makes the associated sheaves agree as fractional submodules on overlaps, so they glue to a coherent sheaf $\mathcal I(D)$ of finite presentation. Its stalk at $y$ is $I_{A_y}(D_y)$ for $A_y=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, a finite rank-one reflexive fractional module. The empty scheme needs no equations and satisfies the conclusion.

source.place: Tag 0EBM, construction of the reflexive module attached to a divisor, applied componentwise.

proof.text: For a geometric point over $y$, the strict-henselization triples theorem identifies $R$ with a local filtered colimit of etale $A_y$-algebras, with local structural map. The existing Noetherianity theorem and normal-domain colimit theorem show that $R$ is a Noetherian normal domain. The existing faithful-flatness theorem makes $A_y\to R$ faithfully flat. Consequently the ind-etale valuation comparison applies to this map.

For an ind-etale map $A\to B$ between the Noetherian normal domains in question, each height-one prime $\mathfrak q$ contracts to a height-one prime $\mathfrak p$, with unchanged normalized valuation. Define the coefficient at $\mathfrak q$ to be $d_{\mathfrak p}$. Only finitely many coefficients are nonzero: $D$ has finite support and the existing finite-separable-fibres lemma gives only finitely many primes of $B$ above each supported prime. This defines $D_B$, and the same argument defines $E_B$. For a tower, contraction of primes is transitive, so the coefficient obtained by two pullbacks equals the coefficient obtained directly; valuations are compatible by composing their equalities. Apply this on the integral affine components of etale neighbourhoods (normality is preserved by etale maps, and their rings are locally Noetherian by the finite-type-algebra Noetherianity lemma, since the etale definition supplies local finite presentation), and to the strict-local map from Step 2. The pulled-back coefficients are exactly the rule in the statement; $D_R=aE_R$.

source.place: Tag 0AH1; coefficient calculation using unchanged normalized valuations. Etale definition and Tag 00FN (algebra-lemma-Noetherian-permanence).

proof.text:
Let $A=A_y$ and $M=\mathcal I(D)_y=I_A(D_y)$. Flatness identifies $M\otimes_A R$ with its image in $\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ (tensor the inclusion $M\subset\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ and then localize). The flat-reflexivity lemma makes this image finite reflexive. At a height-one prime $\mathfrak q\subset R$ over $\mathfrak p$, its localization is $\pi_{\mathfrak p}^{d_{\mathfrak p}}R_{\mathfrak q}$ by the lattice formula and tensor localization. The valuation comparison makes $\pi_{\mathfrak p}$ a uniformizer there. Thus this lattice equals $I_R(D_R)_{\mathfrak q}$. Both fractional modules equal the intersection of their height-one lattices, so
$$\mathcal I(D)_y\otimes_{A_y}R=I_R(D_R).$$
Also, for any normal Noetherian domain $T$ and $c\in\operatorname{Frac}(T)^\times$ with $\operatorname{div}_T(c)=F$, the same lattice formula gives $I_T(F)_{\mathfrak q}=cT_{\mathfrak q}$; taking intersections gives $I_T(F)=cT$. These are direct comparisons of the cited height-one formulas, with no freeness assertion added.

source.place: Tags 0EB9 and 0AVB; compare localized fractional modules, then intersect.

proof.text: If $D$ is Cartier, take its nonzero rational equation $f$ near $y$. The valuation comparison shows that its image $c_{\bar y}$ in $\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ has divisor $D_R$. Conversely, suppose all the required $c_{\bar y}$ exist. Choose a geometric point over each $y$. Step 4 gives $\mathcal I(D)_y\otimes R=c_{\bar y}R$, a free rank-one module. Apply finite-projective descent along the flat local map $A_y\to R$: $\mathcal I(D)_y$ is finite free. Its rank is one because its fraction-field extension has dimension one. The prescribed-stalk-basis spreading lemma gives an open neighbourhood of $y$ with a single basis section $f_y$ of $\mathcal I(D)$. On every height-one stalk there, equality $\mathcal I(D)=f_y\mathcal O$ and the lattice formula force $v(f_y)$ to equal the coefficient of $D$. On overlaps, $f_y\mathcal O=f_z\mathcal O$, so $f_y/f_z$ and its inverse are regular, hence their ratio is a unit. The equations $f_y$ therefore define a Cartier divisor with Weil divisor exactly $D$, proving the equivalence for this fixed $a$.

source.place: Tag 0EBM and Algebra Tag 00O1 (lemma-finite-projective-descends); Modules Tag 0B8J (lemma-finite-presentation-stalk-free).

proof.text: Under these equivalent conditions, suppose $E$ is effective. The coefficients of $D=aE$ and $D_R$ are nonnegative, so the effective-ideal clause gives $I_R(D_R)\subset R$. Step 4 implies $c_{\bar y}\in R\setminus\{0\}$, even for the generators originally supplied. Likewise $\mathcal I(D)\subset\mathcal O_Y$, so the local basis sections $f_y$ are regular and nonzero on their integral components; they are non-zero-divisors. Thus the glued Cartier divisor is effective. On an affine chart its ideal has radical $\bigcap_{am_j>0}\mathfrak p_j$, so its support is the union of those $|Z_j|$. Since $a>0$ this is precisely $\bigcup_{m_j\ne0}|Z_j|$. Each open chart carrying $f_y$ is already an etale neighbourhood of $y$; lift the given geometric point through this open immersion. It has the asserted single non-zero-divisor equation. For $E=0$ the ideal is the whole structure sheaf and one may use the equation $1$, with empty support.

source.place: Tag 0EBM, effective fractional ideals; final equations and support from the lattice formula.

I read the statement of every cited node and the Stacks sources: 0EB9 statement and proof, 0AVB(3), 0AH1, 0EBM, 0B8J. The item statement is unchanged; on the A_1 cone, the fixed multiple a=2 holds and a=1 fails, as the statement predicts. Step 1: clopen components give integral Noetherian normal charts; the localization rule of the lattice lemma glues a finitely presented subsheaf of K. Step 2: triples, Noetherian, normal-domain colimit and faithful flatness give a Noetherian normal domain R with A_y->R injective, local and flat; the pairs definition of the strict henselization is the triples category over m, which is elementary. Step 3: the new ind-etale node gives height and valuation comparison; the 0AH1 node gives finite support; etale charts are covered by etale-normal, the etale definition and 00FN; towers follow from transitivity of contraction. Step 4: flat embedding into Frac R, 0EB9 reflexivity, height-one lattices pi^d R_q, intersection of lattices; the principal case gives I(div c)=cT. Step 5: the flat local finite-projective descent leaf, rank 1, then the 0B8J spread; overlap ratios are units. Step 6: the effective-ideal and radical clauses give c in R, non-zero-divisor equations and support = union of Z_j; Zariski charts serve as etale neighbourhoods; E=0 gives equation 1. All three new nodes are true and statement-only, and none is a duplicate: the nearest nodes are lem-sc-etale-local-dimension, lem-sc-strict-henselization-dimension, lem-sfb-etale-stalk-invariants and lem-sc-divisor-module-local, which give only dimension or curve statements. All declared tool_uses are generic algebra and accepted.
